question: Electric energy consumed in one second is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4 ) power**__

 

Power is a physical quantity that measures the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred or converted per unit of time.

P=(W)/(t)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In (SI), the standard unit of power (P) is the watt (W).
 
• Watt (W) which is defined as one joule of energy per second.
 
• Power can be used to describe the amount of work done, energy consumed, or energy transferred per unit of time.
 
• Power can be expressed in various forms, including mechanical power, electrical power, and thermal power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **There are several different units for measuring power, depending on the context and the system of measurement being used.**

 
 

 **Watt (W)**
 The watt is the SI unit of power. It represents one joule of energy transferred or converted per second. In other words, 1 watt (W) is equal to 1 joule per second (J/s). The relationship is expressed as 1 W = 1 J/s.
 
 

 **Horsepower (hp)**
 Horsepower is a unit of power that is commonly used, especially in the context of mechanical power, particularly in the United States. The relationship between the watt and horsepower is approximately 1 horsepower (hp) is equal to 745.7 watts (W). The conversion factor may vary slightly depending on the standard used.
 
 

 **Kilowatt (kW)**
 The megawatt is an even larger unit used for very high-power applications, such as power plants. One megawatt (MW) is equal to 1,000,000 watts (W). The relationship is expressed as: 1 MW = 1,000,000 W.
 
 

 **Gigawatt (GW)**
 The gigawatt is another larger unit, often used to describe the power output of large power plants or the energy consumption of entire regions. One gigawatt (GW) is equal to 1,000,000,000 watts (W). The relationship is expressed as: 1 GW = 1,000,000,000 W.
 
 

 **Calories per Second**
 In some contexts, especially in nutrition and exercise science, power can be measured in calories per second. One calorie per second (cal/s) is approximately equal to 4.184 watts (W).
 
 

 **BTU per Hour (BTU/hr)**
 In some heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) applications, power is measured in British Thermal Units per hour (BTU/hr). One BTU per hour is roughly equal to 0.293 watts (W).
 
 

 **Megawatt (MW)**
 The megawatt is an even larger unit used for very high power applications, such as power plants. One megawatt (MW) is equal to 1,000,000 watts (W). The relationship is expressed as: 1 MW = 1,000,000 W.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/703977903daa424f3c763dd1c3ba98d6abee6d81573b6d7edfc0e89e207cbf3f.png] 

The unit of power, the "watt," (W) is named after __**James Watt**__, a Scottish engineer and inventor.
